messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT auto-page — cont-batch path p99 spike detected (streaming lane us-west2). p95 ~420ms -> 780ms, p99 ~250ms -> 2.1s in last 5m. Severity: P1. auto-notify eng-oncall.

sam: oncall sam here, pulling traces + packer metrics now.

sam: quick metrics snapshot (prom query):
```
sum(rate(contbatch_requests_total{lane=\"streaming\"}[5m])) by (pool) = 820rps
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(contbatch_request_duration_seconds_bucket{lane=\"streaming\"}[5m])) by (le)) ≈ 2.1
avg_over_time(batch_size{lane=\"streaming\"}[5m]) ≈ 14.7
```

sam: looks like oddpack amplification — average batch size jumped; mixed sequence lengths causing long-tail packing delays. also seeing packer queue depth spikes and some preemption thrash.

lee: confirmed, traces show many short requests getting held behind a few very long seq requests — scheduling fairness not isolating streaming small seqs. KV cache misses also higher for these traces.

maya: any customer impact so far? paging from SLOs but need to know if clients see 5xxs or slow responses.

sam: error rate for streaming endpoints up from 0.2% -> 1.6% for last 10m. top affected customer: customer-x (premium) — 12 ops with >1s tail responses, no widespread 5xx flood.

jules: pinged CS to flag customer-x and set expectation. will send short email + Slack DM.

sam: immediate mitigations I can try:
- cap streaming packer batch_size to 8 (drops packing delay)
- enable preemptive-shed for >512 tokens on cont-batch path for streaming lane
- route new streaming requests to non-batched runtime (single-shot) for critical customers
- add temporary priority for short sequences in scheduler (heuristic: seq_len < 128)

lee: +1 for cap and seq-priority. packer config change should be low-risk. single-shot fallback is safest for customer impact but increases cost.

sam: applying cap now. command:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap packer-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"streaming.max_batch_size":"8"}}'
```

[ops-bot] deploy-bot: rolling restart triggered for packer-pods in us-west2 (3 pods).

sam: restart in progress, watching p99.

sam: post-change metrics (2m after):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(contbatch_request_duration_seconds_bucket{lane=\"streaming\"}[2m])) by (le)) ≈ 580ms
avg batch_size ≈ 7.1
queue_depth 95p reduced from 320 -> 60
```

sam: p99 dropped significantly — appears to help. error rate still slightly elevated (1.2%) but trending down.

maya: great. can we enable seq priority asap and monitor? that should reduce re-amplification while packers rebalance.

lee: posting proposed scheduler tweak:
```json
{"scheduler":{"streaming":{"priority_by_seq_len":true,"seq_len_threshold":128}}}
```
(note: applying as lightweight toggle).

sam: applying seq-priority patch now.

pagerduty-bot: user sam acknowledged the page. status: investigating.

sam: seq-priority live. verifying metrics..

sam: metrics (1m after): p99 ~420ms, p95 ~360ms, avg batch_size ~6.4, decoupled short-seq tail traces show much fewer waits.

jules: CS updated customer-x, asked to route their traffic to single-shot for 30m while we monitor. they approved.

maya: can we do single-shot routing only for customer-x (header match) to minimize cost?

lee: yes. router rule: if header X-Client-ID==customer-x then runtime=single_shot. push in 5m.

sam: queued routing rule change. applying now.

[ops-bot] config-bot: router rule applied for customer-x -> single_shot.

sam: after all mitigations (batch cap, seq-priority, customer single-shot) system p99 settled ~380ms for streaming. error rates back to 0.3%.

maya: good stabilization. next actions:
- monitor p95/p99 for 30m, watch for re-amplification patterns
- collect sample traces for postmortem (priority: cont-batch traces + scheduler logs)
- run small experiment to tune max_batch_size (8->6->10) during off-peak to find cost/latency sweet spot
- SRE to consider adding fairness token for streaming lane in scheduler (hard guardrails)

sam: I'll keep eye on dashboards for 30m and capture trace set. adding runbook note: temp cap + seq-priority toggled.

jules: I'll keep CS looped and draft customer-facing blurb summarizing cause + mitigation.

lee: we should schedule a short postmortem with research/serving team to decide long-term changes: better packer heuristics, dynamic batch caps by seq-length distribution, and KV cache warming for long sequences.

maya: taking on-call handoff at +30m if stable. I'll post formal handoff message then.

sam: thanks all. feels like immediate risk mitigated. :thumbsup:

[30m later]

maya: taking over monitoring. everything looks stable: p99 trending 330-420ms. leaving the packer cap and seq-priority enabled for now. setting alert thresholds tighter to catch re-occurrence.

maya: handoff notes: root cause likely scheduling-induced oddpack amplification from mixed sequence lengths on streaming lane; mitigations we ran: packer max_batch_size=8, scheduler priority_by_seq_len=true, customer-x routed to single_shot. Postmortem owners: sam (serving), lee (scheduler), jules (CS).

jules: acknowledged, will prep customer comms and postmortem template.

ops-bot: incident closed to P2 (stabilized). recommend postmortem. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks team, will run follow-up and postmortem doc tomorrow.

sam: adding final logs + traces to the incident board.

lee: saving scheduler diff + packer config to /incidents/1717733333-oddpack-stream-stall for postmortem.

jules: closing customer loop if no regressions in next 24h.

pagerduty-bot: incident ticket updated, severity lowered.

maya: end of thread.
